title: Symphony No. 9 in E minor, “From the New World”
hook: A Czech composer’s postcard from America, written with homesickness in the ink.

painting.title: Among the Sierra Nevada, California
painting.collection: Smithsonian American Art Museum, Washington, D.C.
painting.pairingNote: The vast, luminous American landscape as a European-trained artist imagined it, which is exactly what Dvořák did in sound.

facts: Written in New York in the first half of 1893, while Dvořák directed the National Conservatory of Music. First performed at Carnegie Hall on 16 December 1893.
Dvořák was fascinated by African American spirituals and by Longfellow’s poem “The Song of Hiawatha”, which he said inspired the two middle movements.
The famous slow-movement tune is Dvořák’s own. The words “Goin’ Home” were added by a pupil almost thirty years later.
Themes from earlier movements keep returning in later ones, and all of them meet in the finale.
bigPicture.inOneLine: arrival and energy (I), longing for home (II), a dance in the forest (III), everything gathered together (IV).

movements.heading: Adagio – Allegro molto
movements.summary: A brooding slow introduction, then a [[sonata-form|sonata form]] movement with three themes, each as memorable as a folk song.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a horn call that leaps up and falls back. It will return in every movement.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a rustic, slightly sad dance for flute and oboe.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 3
mainIdeas.description: a gentle tune for solo flute, low and warm, which many hear as an echo of the spiritual “Swing Low, Sweet Chariot”.

stops.hear: Quiet low strings; then sudden shocks from horns, strings and drums
Horns leap up and fall back; woodwinds answer with a bouncing rhythm
Flute and oboe in a folk-like tune over a droning bass
A solo flute, low and gentle
The flute tune and the horn call, broken up and passed around
The horn call returns

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: Trumpets and trombones blaze out the horn call

movements.heading: Largo
movements.summary: One of the best-loved melodies in all music, sung by an instrument that rarely gets the spotlight: the English horn.

stops.hear: Slow, solemn chords in the brass, moving through strange harmonies
English horn over [[muted|muted]] strings
A slightly faster, plaintive tune in flute and oboe; plucked basses walk beneath
stops.happening: The middle section, in the minor. Dvořák linked it to a funeral in the forest from “Hiawatha”

stops.hear: Oboe and flute chirp brightly; the music swells; trombones thunder out the horn call from the first movement
stops.happening: A sudden vision of daylight, and the first movement breaks in

stops.hear: The English horn melody returns
A handful of solo strings take the tune. It stops. Silence. It tries again
stops.happening: The melody falters twice, as if overcome

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The solemn brass chords; then a soft chord for double basses alone

notice: The pauses near the end are written into the score. The silence is the homesickness.

movements.heading: Scherzo: Molto vivace
movements.summary: A fast, rhythmic [[scherzo|scherzo]] with a triangle, which Dvořák said was suggested by a dance at the wedding feast in “Hiawatha”. The middle is pure Bohemia.

stops.hear: Sharp chords and a drum figure; then a darting tune in the woodwinds
stops.happening: The scherzo. The opening tips its hat to the scherzo of Beethoven’s Ninth

stops.hear: The pace relaxes into a lilting woodwind melody
stops.happening: A gentler second idea, in the major

stops.hear: Cellos quietly recall the horn call from the first movement
A swaying, waltz-like tune in the woodwinds with trilling strings
stops.happening: The [[trio|trio]]. This is a Czech village dance, not an American one

stops.hear: The darting tune returns

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: The horn call from the first movement, fading away, then one loud chord

movements.heading: Allegro con fuoco
movements.summary: A blazing march theme, and then a grand reunion: melodies from all three earlier movements return and are woven together.

stops.hear: Strings push upward, two notes at a time, faster and faster
Trumpets and horns blaze out a bold march
A single soft cymbal clash
stops.happening: The only note the cymbals play in the whole symphony

stops.hear: A clarinet sings a long, tender melody over shimmering strings
The Largo tune in the woodwinds, the scherzo’s darting tune, the horn call from the first movement
stops.happening: The [[development|development]]. The earlier movements come back one after another

stops.hear: The march returns, at first surprisingly quietly
The solemn chords that opened the Largo, now fortissimo in the brass

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The march and the first movement’s horn call at the same time

stops.label: Last chord
stops.hear: The winds hold the final chord and let it fade to nothing
stops.happening: Instead of a bang, the symphony ends by dying away

notice: Count the returning themes in the finale. By the end, all four movements are present.

threads.title: The horn call
threads.body: Theme 1 of the first movement appears in every movement.

threads.title: Two homes
threads.body: American inspiration (spirituals, “Hiawatha”) in a thoroughly Czech musical accent.

threads.title: A gathered ending
threads.body: The finale brings every movement’s main theme back.
